topic: What happens if you climb Mount Everest?
title: What climbing Everest does
hook: What happens if you climb Mount Everest?

beats.label: 0 M
beats.line: At sea level, every breath is full of oxygen.

beats.label: 3000 M
beats.line: By three thousand meters, the air thins, and you breathe faster.

beats.label: 5000 M
beats.line: At five thousand meters, your heart pounds to find more oxygen.

beats.label: 7000 M
beats.line: By seven thousand meters, thin air can bring on a pounding headache.

beats.label: 8849 M
beats.line: At the summit, each breath has only a third of the oxygen.

end.line: So, could you handle that thin summit air?

description: Checkpoint by checkpoint, how thinning air pushes the body toward its limit.

facts.claim: Air pressure and oxygen availability drop as altitude increases.
Acute mountain sickness (headache, nausea, fatigue) can occur above about 2,500 meters.
The body raises heart rate and breathing rate to compensate for lower oxygen at altitude.
At the summit of Mount Everest (8,849 m), available oxygen is roughly a third of sea-level amounts.
